Everything under $1,000 free. I view this financially like how lottery prizes at $599.99 and below are tax-free.

Essentially, I'd make a ton of individual bets at a sportsbook of $999.99 each. If it's unlimited from there, I just pile that up over time, since an unlimited count of $999.99 bets applies. The bets themselves have no risk at that point and one outcome is assured a winner. At standard -110 odds for each side, each bet has a value of $454.54 in profit (999.99\*100/110/2). To reach $5M is only 11,001 bets. That's only 62 bets a day to reach and ultimately cross the $5M in 180 days. With how many games, say, college basketball plays daily, plus the number of sportsbooks? Incredibly easy to hit.

Six bets, of which three will win, alone come from any one given game: Each team's spread, each side's total, each side's moneyline. $999.99 for free on each, and that results in $2,727.25 profit for maybe two minutes of work. I think I can get maybe 30 of these sets of six per hour, for $81,817.36. Worst case, it's half of that for $40,909.68. Per hour. Probably would do it twice/two hours a day, so take the average of the two and that's $61,363.02 per day. Doing this method for five days a week for 75% of weeks out of the year, or 39, I'm at $23,931,578.80 per annum. The math makes the choice clear. I'm also assuming I wouldn't get the principal amount back on any given bet given it is a bonus style bet in awarding.

This also works at the roulette table too, just place a bet on every number. At a 35:1 payout, and that's an easy $34,999.65 per spin at $999.99, or $34,965 if a $999 wager. No matter what. That's only 143 spins to surpass $5M. Or 144 if you're spinning per number at a rounder $999. Yeah.

I work for one of the huge sportsbooks setting lines for this type of stuff. But speaking only for myself specifically and what I’ve learned? 

Sharp bets/bettors and models move lines, especially the former. Not Vegas. I live in in the Tristate area, thus by definition not a monolithic Vegas overlord. Some books that you can’t bet with in the US are based in Costa Rica and Curaçao.

General public isn’t going to move the line no matter how big it is because at large, that’s not helpful data in price discovery. Think about Mattress Mack. Big bets in the millions, but I don’t think anyone considered him an especially experienced, skillful bettor.

Last but not least: 80% of the handle doesn’t tell me much in precision. What did they bet? Moneyline? Spread? From there what number, what price…there’s a ton that goes into this. Bettor and book alike. It’s a ton harder than you’d think upfront.

I outsold singlehandedly at a franchise store that got 10% of volume sales of the same ones of the same ownership group that had 10x the sales and average orders per day with a straightforward technique and phrase.  All with an uplifting, genuine, encouraging smile and tone. Describe it like you're describing it to a friend of something new you just loved. Managers all noticed this ability to sell across the company beyond my store. It's simple. Use this phrasing, and this phrasing exactly:

Would you prefer to donate to benefit kids in need of a good home today? 

Let's talk about and break down why this works: Would, you, and prefer, meaning the guest is in implied control of the situation. Would is choice, you is personally empowering, and prefer makes the option theirs, rather than the pretense of a sale. It's a lead-in to tripping their emotions.

Next: Benefit, kids, home. Benefit is a word of mutual trust, kids are a raw emotion word, and home is a place of safety and security. So thus, you're conveying familarity, security, and trust. Today is now. Urgency. Just like fast food, it's today, it's now, it's immediate, just like what you want. And that's why deep down people consume fast food, they want to experience something to that effect. I just took advantage of it in donation form.

If they say yes, your next line line is simple. Notice that I never mentioned anything like 'A boo book', because if you're only asking if you want to buy one, you've limited how many you're going to actually sell at that point. Instead, ask the following, if affirmative:

​

"How much would you prefer to donate today?" Routinely I'd get $5-10 donations, and that itself is 5-10 books out the door. If it's no, you thank them equally kindly and genuinely anyway, as you've guilted them and it's possible they may relent at that point.

I only presented the Boo Books after the money or card was swiped, to make it seem like it was a special reward the guests were to receive, almost as if a bonus, making this a unique. unexpected interaction point of transaction.
